title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google
summary:
But the UK AI minister admitted last week that figure was significantly higher than the government’s actual projections after it was revealed that the assessment came solely from a report commissioned by Google and that its own estimation of AI’s economic benefit was less than a third of that £400 billion figure.
AI minister Kanishka Narayan, answering a parliamentary question on the issue, said that AI adoption and data investment could add £55 billion to £140 billion to the UK economy by 2030, bringing the central estimate to £120 billion.
Narayan said the £400 billion figure “was drawn from a publicly available 2023 report commissioned by Google and produced by Public First,” a British consultancy firm now referred to as PF Global.
“AI is a very fast-moving technology, and, as we learn more, we inevitably have to update the assumptions lying behind our models.
The answer did not withdraw the £400 billion figure or say it had been wrong.

title: Stock market today: Dow plunges 1,800 points, Nasdaq enters correction in AI trade meltdown
summary:
US stocks plunged on Thursday as AI and chip stocks sold off, erasing the gains from Wednesday's post-election rally.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) tumbled 3.4%, or more than 1,800 points.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 4.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) dropped 5.5%, with the tech-heavy index closing in correction territory.
Wall Street unloaded this year's AI winners, while large-cap tech stocks saw the worst day since the COVID-19 pandemic sell-off.
Oil prices rose amid uncertainty that President Trump would pursue a deal with Iran to end the war in the Middle East.

title: Stock market today: Dow surges 1,500 points in best day of 2026, S&P 500 and Nasdaq rally after historic midterm election
summary:
US stocks jumped on Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in a seismic midterm election, paving the way for a divided government.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) rose 3%, or over 1,500 points, marking its best single-day performance since President Trump paused a sweeping tariff rollout in April 2025.
Oil prices plunged as the midterm election outcome also raised hopes for an end to the war in the Middle East.
On the economic front, ISM and S&P data showed that US services activity expanded at a slower pace in October as businesses continued to grapple with elevated costs.
AMD ( AMD ) posted a Q3 earnings beat , while McDonald's ( MCD ) grappled with slowing same-store sales growth.

title: Why are wealthy countries failing developing nations?
summary:
UN report warns climate adaptation funding is falling far short of needsThe United Nations Environment Programme has published a report warning that the world is not adapting quickly enough to keep pace with the growing human and economic costs linked to the climate crisis.
The UN singles out wealthy countries – responsible for the bulk of carbon emissions – for failing to meet their financial pledges.
At successive Conference of the Parties (COP) meetings, billions of dollars have been earmarked to help developing nations become more resilient.
But only a fraction has been paid out.
